summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin, a British-American astronomer and astrophysicist. It gives her lifespan (May 10, 1900 to December 7, 1979) and her key contribution: a 1925 Ph.D. thesis proposing that stellar composition is explained by the relative abundances of hydrogen and helium.
one_line: Biographical note on Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin, the British-American astronomer whose 1925 thesis linked stellar composition to hydrogen and helium abundances.
key_facts: Cecilia Helena Payne-Gaposchkin was born on May 10, 1900.
Cecilia Helena Payne-Gaposchkin died on December 7, 1979.
Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin was a British-American astronomer and astrophysicist.
In 1925, Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin proposed in her Ph.D. thesis an explanation for the composition of stars.
Her 1925 thesis explained stellar composition in terms of the relative abundances of hydrogen and helium.

entities.role: British-American astronomer and astrophysicist who proposed in her 1925 Ph.D. thesis that stellar composition reflects the relative abundances of hydrogen and helium
